prose:
A CLI named `tool`. One command: `greet`. It takes a required option `--name` (a string).
On success print exactly one line: greet|name=<name>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command reached as `db migrate`. It takes a required option `--to` (a string).
On success print exactly one line: migrate|to=<to>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `open`, which takes ONE POSITIONAL argument called `path` (not an option).
Invoked as `tool open ./src`. On success print exactly one line: open|path=<path>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `list`, taking ONE OPTIONAL trailing positional argument `scope` that defaults to `all`.
Invoked as `tool list` or `tool list mine`. Print exactly one line: list|scope=<scope>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `build`. It has a PRESENCE-ONLY flag `--verbose` (passing it takes no value; omitting it means off).
Print exactly one line: build|verbose=<on|off>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `sync`. It has an option `--force` that is an explicit TWO-STATE boolean: the user types `--force true` or `--force false`. It defaults to false when omitted.
Print exactly one line: sync|force=<true|false>  (lowercase) and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `tag`. It has an option `--tag` that may be REPEATED to collect several values.
Print exactly one line: tag|tags=<comma-joined values in the order given>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `shard`. It has a KEY-VALUE (dictionary) option `--set`, invoked as `--set[eu] 3 --set[us] 5`, producing a mapping from string keys to int values.
Print exactly one line: shard|<key>=<value> pairs sorted by key and joined by commas, e.g. shard|eu=3,us=5  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `wait`. It has an option `--for` holding a duration, which an operator may type as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".
Print exactly one line: wait|seconds=<total whole seconds>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `log`. It has an option `--level` whose value is one of an enum: Debug, Info, Warn, Error.
Print exactly one line: log|level=<level>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. TWO commands sharing a prefix: `cache clear` and `cache stats`. Neither takes options.
Print exactly one line: cache-clear  or  cache-stats  respectively, and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `seed`. It has an option `--rows` (an integer) that defaults to 10 when omitted.
Print exactly one line: seed|rows=<rows>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command shaped `copy <source> <dest>` where source and dest are POSITIONAL arguments.
Invoked as `tool copy a.txt b.txt`. Print exactly one line: copy|from=<source>|to=<dest>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command shaped `user <id> delete` — the positional argument sits BETWEEN two literal words.
Invoked as `tool user 42 delete`. Print exactly one line: delete|id=42  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `push`. It has a required string option with BOTH a long form `--remote` and a short form `-r`.
Print exactly one line: push|remote=<remote>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `fetch`, whose handler is ASYNCHRONOUS (it awaits something) and takes a required option `--url`.
Print exactly one line: fetch|url=<url>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `check`. It takes a required integer option `--code`. The command prints exactly one line: check|code=<code>  and then EXITS WITH THAT NUMBER as the process exit code.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `page`. It has THREE related options that should be grouped into a single reusable options class rather than three separate handler parameters: `--offset` (int, default 0), `--limit` (int, default 50), and `--sort` (string, default "id").
Print exactly one line: page|offset=<offset>|limit=<limit>|sort=<sort>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command: `ping`. It has an option `--endpoint` (string). When `--endpoint` is not passed, its value must come from the environment variable `TOOL_ENDPOINT`. If neither is present it defaults to `local`.
Print exactly one line: ping|endpoint=<endpoint>  and exit 0.

A CLI named `tool`. One command reached as `remote branch delete` (three literal words) taking a required option `--name`.
Print exactly one line: rbd|name=<name>  and exit 0.
